'''Georges André Sentenac''' (born 4 May 1939) is a French [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] specializing in [[Transcription (biology)|gene transcription]].

Married to Pierrette Balse, professor of [[mathematics]] at the University of [[Orsay]], they had three children, all scientists, Anne, Marion and Daniel.

== Biography ==
He was elected correspondent of the French Academy of sciences in 1999 and then a member of the Institute in 2007.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-S/andre-sentenac.html|publication-date=}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
During his postdoctoral internship in Dr. George Acs' laboratory in New York City, Sentenac addresses the regulation of gene expression by showing that appropriate hormonal treatment forces a young male cockerel to produce certain specific components of the egg. Back in France, to bypass the complexity of higher organisms, he chose to work on the [[yeast]] [[Saccharomyces cerevisiae]]. In the following years, this yeast will become an essential study model in the molecular genetics of eukaryotic cells.

First, he isolated and identified the essential components of the molecular machinery responsible for [[gene transcription]] in yeast. He gave the first complete description of the three forms of nuclear [[RNA polymerase]]s which are composed of the assembly of many subunits with various functions.<ref>Sentenac, A., « Eukaryotic RNA polymerases », ''CRC Crit. Rev. Biochem.'', (1985), 18, <abbr>p.</abbr> 31-90</ref> Focusing his efforts on the transcription of the large family of class III genes encoding [[Transfer RNA|tRNAs]], [[5S ribosomal RNA|5S RNA]] and other small [[RNA]]s, he isolated the general transcription factors TFIIIC and TFIIIB and described the cascade of protein-DNA and protein-protein interaction leading to the recruitment of RNA polymerase III on DNA and the initiation of transcription.<ref name=":1">Chédin, S., et al., « The yeast RNA polymerase III transcription machinery: a paradigm for eukaryotic gene activation », ''Cold Spring Harb. Symp. Quant. Biol.'', (1998), 63, <abbr>p.</abbr> 381-389</ref> A total of 26 proteins are dedicated to the transcription of class III genes. In particular, it shows that the TFIIIC factor consists of two protein modules capable of binding to two distinct promoter elements spaced differently according to genes,<ref>Marzouki, N., et al., « Selective proteolysis defines two DNA binding domains in yeast transcription factor τ. », ''Nature'', (1986), 323, <abbr>p.</abbr> 176-178</ref> of lifting chromatin repression and of recruiting TFIIIB.<ref name=":1" /><ref>Burnol, et al., « TFIIIC relieves repression of U6 snRNA transcription by chromatin », ''Nature'', (993), 62, <abbr>p.</abbr> 475-477</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
*1969, Maurice Nicloux Prize of the French Society of Biochemistry{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
*1977, Paul Doisteau-Emile Blutel Prize from the Academy of Sciences{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
*1985, Elected Member of [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]]<ref>{{cite web|title=EMBO|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/andre-sentenac|publication-date=}}</ref>
*1987, [[CNRS Silver Medal]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Médaille d'argent du CNRS|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/talents/cnrs?medal=39|publication-date=}}</ref>
*1997, Charles-Léopold Mayer Grand Prize of the French Academy of sciences{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
*1999, Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Academia europaea|url=https://wikimonde.com/article/Academia_Europaea|publication-date=}}</ref>
*1999, Correspondent of the French Academy of sciences<ref name=":0" />
*1999-2004, Member of the EMBO Council{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
*2007, Member of the French Academy of sciences<ref name=":0" />
*2012, Commander in the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques|Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
*2018, Officer in the Ordre de la [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'Honneur]]{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}
